newsitem.title: FRANCE: Disenchanted Council of Europe aide to quit.
newsitem.headline: Disenchanted Council of Europe aide to quit.

text.p: The number two man at the Council of Europe said in an interview published on Thursday he was resigning in disenchantment at a lowering of human rights standards for new east European members.

Peter Leuprecht, Austrian deputy secretary-general of the 40-nation body which promotes democracy and human rights, told Les Dernieres Nouvelles d'Alsace that the organisation had taken in ex-communist states too fast and uncritically.

"When you hear Croatian Foreign Minister (Mate) Granic in the council of ministers saying his country is a model democracy which respects minority rights, and nobody breathes a word...that's the soggy consensus," he said.
Leuprecht, a lawyer who had been director of the Strasbourg-based Council's human rights department, said he would leave his post in September, a year early.
"I have always seen the Council of Europe as a community of values...But now references to democracy and human rights have been reduced to a ritual," he said.
He said the pan-European institution, often regarded as an antechamber to the European Union, had enlarged too fast at the price of a dilution of its values.
"Some admissions still stick in my throat," he said, without naming any country.

Among the most controversial decisions were the admission of Russia during the war in Chechnya and of Croatia, despite widespread criticism of state domination of the media and attempts to curtail the rights of the political opposition.
On the other hand, Leuprecht praised efforts made by Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovenia to adapt their legislation to the European Convention on Human Rights.
